the_five_links.1_t_is_zeta6: m004's holonomy parameter satisfies t^2 = t - 1, hence t^6 = 1 and t^3 = -1: a primitive 6th root. Its square t^2 = omega is a primitive cube root.
the_five_links.2_Phi3: Phi3(u) = u^2 + u + 1 vanishes at omega and at omega^2 -- B1200's polynomial, reached from m004's own holonomy rather than from the partition function
the_five_links.3_linking_map: u -> u^2 sends omega to omega^2 and omega^2 back to omega: the SWAP, and an involution on the two roots
the_five_links.4_swap_is_conjugation: omega^2 = conjugate(omega), so the swap IS complex conjugation on Q(sqrt-3), i.e. the nontrivial element of Gal(Q(sqrt-3)/Q)
the_five_links.5_conjugation_is_the_mirror: conj(t) = 1 - t, the other root; the conjugated holonomy satisfies the SAME relator, so Galois acts on the character variety and complex conjugation of the representation is orientation reversal

what_it_buys.B1184_is_derived_not_asserted: 'the self-report is complete except exactly one bit, and the bit is c' now names the SAME bit as the orientation obstruction, via this identification rather than by coincidence of labels
what_it_buys.paper_IV_is_inside_the_unification: Paper IV's orbit theorem obstructs selection within a G-orbit for G = Z/2 the mirror. That G is c. So the paper's obstruction concerns the same involution that links B1200's saddle, founding obstruction and boundary.
what_it_buys.the_observer_bit_is_named_concretely: the orientation the object cannot self-supply is the choice between omega and omega^2 -- a choice of root of Phi3, simultaneously the saddle branch, the conjugate pair of the founding obstruction, and the boundary's Coxeter class

why: reading main after reactivation, B1200 unified three faces under Phi3 with linking map u -> u^2 = the Galois generator c. Paper IV's orbit theorem runs on G = Z/2 generated by the mirror. I flagged the possible identification and did not assert it; this verifies it.
